segments.title: HMS Orion's battle honours, 1939-44
segments.summary: HMS Orion's honours span Atlantic service in 1939, Mediterranean campaigns from Calabria to Salerno, and 1944 operations in Normandy and southern France.
segments.body: HMS Orion's honours open with Atlantic service in 1939 and Calabria and Mediterranean service in 1940. The 1941 list includes Malta convoy duty, Matapan, Greece and Crete, which makes the missing general Mediterranean honour for that year seem curious. Sicily and Salerno follow in 1943. The 1944 honours cover the Aegean, Anzio, Normandy and southern France. The list shows how often the Royal Navy committed this Leander-class cruiser across several theatres.

evidence.note: The transcript lists Orion's Atlantic, Mediterranean, Greek, Italian, Aegean, Normandy and southern-France battle honours.

segments.title: What battle-honour totals hide
segments.summary: Comparisons with HMS Nubian, HMS Jervis and Warspite show why battle-honour totals do not rank warships on equal terms.
segments.body: Orion officially matches HMS Nubian and HMS Jervis and trails only Warspite. That comparison needs a qualification: the rules treated ship types differently. A battleship could receive an honour simply for being present and firing its guns, while a cruiser or destroyer had to do more to qualify. Smaller warships also received campaign honours that could cover several battles instead of counting each action separately. Orion's total therefore says less about the breadth of her service than a simple ship-by-ship tally suggests. The closing verdict calls her a war hero and says she was gone too soon.

evidence.note: The transcript compares Orion with Nubian, Jervis and Warspite, then explains the different battle and campaign-honour treatment of battleships, cruisers and destroyers.
